source.title: The distance between the weights of the neural network is meaningful
source.authors: Li-Qun Yang; Yi-Jun Yang; Yao Wang; Zhenyu Yang; Wei Zeng

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling affecting the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses label corruption and runs its own experiment on a weight-distance information proxy, but it does not measure the training error, test error, or fitting behavior named by any claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for fitting randomized labels, but that cited result is not this study's result. Its own label-corruption experiment measures a weight-distance proxy, not fitting or generalization.
record.test_reason: The study measures weight distance under label corruption, not training error, test error, time to fit, or the order of learning real and noisy labels. Its statements about random-label fitting and slower convergence report Zhang et al.'s results. The authors' interpretation of their proxy does not establish or refute any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose weight distance as an estimate of information accumulated during training and interpret their corruption experiment as showing that corruption hinders learning. They also acknowledge that the method's applicability to overfitting requires further research and that information rankings across architectures do not match expectations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a weight-distance and quasi-Monte Carlo method to estimate information accumulation; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that information quantity rankings across different network structures do not match expectations and may be affected by differing training configurations and model capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: For the TensorFlow CNN Demo on CIFAR-10 trained for equal time, the authors interpret Figure 7 as showing less accumulated information with increasing label corruption, using their weight-distance proxy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label corruption reduces the information accumulation estimated by this study's weight-distance method under its fixed training conditions.

record.problems: The label-corruption finding is reported through a figure without numerical values or uncertainty. The measured proxy does not establish training or test performance.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test performance on completely random labels with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Time required to fit random versus true labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across increasing label corruption.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized.

record.verdict_notes: Equal training duration does not establish equal convergence or time to fit. Weight-distance trajectories do not distinguish learning shared patterns from memorizing noisy labels.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks fit completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, have chance test error, and do so without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time to fit true versus random labels and how convergence time varies with corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training error and test error across label-corruption levels, including whether fitting remains perfect and test error rises steadily.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect fitting random labels or generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, and whether those labels are learned differently over training.

rows.subject: TensorFlow CNN Demo
rows.operation_detail: Trained from the same initial weights on CIFAR-10 datasets with randomly shuffled label fractions, within the same time; measured weight distance.
rows.measure: Distance d(wi, w), used by the paper as a proxy for information accumulated during training.
rows.value: The authors state that increasing label error rate means less information is accumulated and that label corruption hinders learning; the plotted values are figure only.
rows.locator: Application: impact of label corruption; Experiment 4; Figure 7
rows.note: This proxy does not report training error, test error, or whether the networks fit the corrupted labels. The figure's numerical values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The uncorrupted dataset A0 provides a comparison condition, so the baseline should identify 0% shuffled labels. Experiment 4 defines the distance between current and final weights, rather than directly measuring fitting. The protocol inconsistently specifies eleven datasets but ten networks; Figure 7 lists eleven corruption conditions. Numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
